rows.title: CT House Republicans offer $54.4 billion two-year budget plan
rows.standfirst: The CT House Republicans’ budget plan would trim electric rates, bolster schools, freeze wages and cut care for undocumented residents.

rows.title: Union sets May 19 strike deadline at 51 nursing homes
rows.standfirst: SEIU 1199NE wants to boost starting pay for nursing home workers in CT to $25 per hour and, over several years, to about $30 per hour.

rows.title: Budget panel endorses raises for CT troopers
rows.standfirst: The tentative deal had strong bipartisan support, despite recent calls from Republican leaders to freeze wages for all CT state employees.

rows.title: As strike deadline looms, CT nursing homes face added costs
rows.standfirst: The cost of preparing for a threatened May 19 strike at 51 Connecticut nursing homes runs into the millions, an official said.

rows.title: Union pushes CT nursing home strike deadline back to May 27
rows.standfirst: The state’s largest health care workers’ union agreed to push a May 19 strike deadline at 51 Connecticut nursing homes back until May 27.

rows.title: Education aid becoming key to solving CT’s budget puzzle
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly must overcome unprecedented challenges to adopt a new budget, but the biggest hurdle now involves local schools.

rows.title: CT officials poised to exceed budget cap to end Medicaid crisis
rows.standfirst: Officials plan to legally exceed CT’s spending cap to avert a Medicaid crisis and pave the way for a new two-year budget.

rows.title: One skirmish over the CT budget is over, but the big battle looms
rows.standfirst: Last week’s deal among Gov. Ned Lamont and Democrats solved one problem but sets the stage for budget battles that could continue for years.

rows.title: CT legislature approves bill to cover Medicaid shortfall
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers approved a bill to cover CT’s overspending, with Gov. Ned Lamont declaring the first spending cap emergency since 2007.

rows.title: CT state police contract: House approves raises for troopers
rows.standfirst: The proposal to boost pay by an effective 4.5% had bipartisan support despite objections from GOP leaders and is expected to pass the Senate.

rows.title: Key things have changed since CT last exceeded the spending cap
rows.standfirst: To say Connecticut’s government is better prepared to handle a spending cap exception now than it was in 2007 is an understatement.

rows.title: CT nursing home, group home strikes called off after deal reached
rows.standfirst: The SEIU 1199 president said a deal reached with the Lamont administration involved ‘meaningful progress on a pathway to $30’ per hour.

rows.title: CT child tax credit still possible as budget talks hit home stretch
rows.standfirst: Democratic leaders are cautiously optimistic about one popular tax-cutting idea: A $150-per-child tax credit, up to $450 per household.

rows.title: Spending cap will temper big investments in next CT budget
rows.standfirst: Will CT Democrats accept a budget that makes far more modest investments in health care and social services than they promised?

rows.title: CT legislators discuss ditching 2-year budget as priorities clash
rows.standfirst: CT Democrats want to spend $200 million more than Gov. Ned Lamont will accept in 2026-27. Lamont said a one-year plan would be ‘a mistake.’

rows.title: CT budget fight hinges on cutting higher ed reserves
rows.standfirst: Legislative leaders could resolve the budget dispute with Gov. Ned Lamont by making CT public colleges and universities tap their reserves.

rows.title: CT lawmakers scrap child tax credit for middle class — again
rows.standfirst: As session nears closing day, lawmakers negotiate $200 tax break for working poor with kids, but scrap middle class child tax credit

frame: Fixed public category union, followed by frozen economic-title inclusion screen
